title: Pass by value: the most common misunderstanding in Java

videos.script: Ask a room of Java programmers how Java passes arguments, and many will say: primitives by value, objects by reference. The first half is right. The second half is the most common misunderstanding in the language, and twenty-nine lessons have set it up. {{swap}} This lesson starts with a swap that does nothing. Two numbers go into a method, change places inside it, and come out exactly as they went in. {{refs}} Then objects. A method can change the object you gave it, and you see the change. But give its parameter a new object, and you see nothing at all. Both facts have one explanation, and a drawing makes it plain. {{myths}} Then six small experiments, one per belief people hold. A string, an Integer, a swap of two objects, an array and two lists. {{living}} Last, what to do about it: return what you mean to return. By the end there is one rule, and it has no exceptions.
